findings.issue_text: Reminder cancellation promises in handleCancelBooking.ts and the modified rescheduling and workflow handlers are neither awaited nor included in prismaPromises, allowing handlers to return before cleanup finishes and serverless termination to leave reminders active for cancelled bookings.
A failed SendGrid cancellation in scheduleEmailReminders.ts aborts the cancellation loop, leaving subsequent reminders uncancelled and allowing their emails to be sent.
A failed SendGrid cancellation in scheduleEmailReminders.ts skips Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete), leaving successfully cancelled reminders in the database.

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A failed SendGrid cancellation in scheduleEmailReminders.ts aborts the cancellation loop, leaving subsequent reminders uncancelled and allowing their emails to be sent.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the scheduleEmailReminders.ts diff, the code iterates through remindersToCancel in a for loop. For each reminder, it calls `await client.request(...)` to cancel via SendGrid API, then pushes a delete operation to workflowRemindersToDelete array. The entire loop is wrapped in a try-catch block. If the SendGrid API call fails for any reminder, the catch block will be triggered, logging the error and exiting the try block. This means subsequent reminders in the loop won't be processed - they won't be cancelled via SendGrid and won't be added to the delete array. The finding correctly identifies that a single SendGrid API failure will abort processing of all remaining reminders in the batch, potentially leaving them uncancelled and allowing their emails to be sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A failed SendGrid cancellation in scheduleEmailReminders.ts skips Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete), leaving successfully cancelled reminders in the database.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in scheduleEmailReminders.ts, the loop iterates through remindersToCancel and for each reminder: (1) calls client.request to cancel via SendGrid API, (2) creates a delete promise and pushes to workflowRemindersToDelete array. The entire block is wrapped in a single try-catch. If the SendGrid API call fails for any reminder, the catch block is triggered and execution jumps out of the loop, meaning Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete) is never called. This means any reminders that were successfully cancelled before the failure will not have their database records deleted, leaving orphaned records. This is a real bug - partial success leaves inconsistent state.
